summary: Improved the framework to keep each product memory local and identity-bound; no real product repositories were migrated.
completed_work: Added explicit init/start/close project-memory entry point with project identity and origin binding.
Reused canonical builders against explicit target roots and kept product/framework versions separate.
Added local Obsidian views with edit protection and freshness reporting.
Excluded upstream memory and product views from adoption plans; rejected product repositories as distribution sources.
Tested two independent Git projects and fresh-process resume without changing framework state.
validation: Final release validation passed all 46 gates, including 363 tests, 14 policies and cumulative/recovery/incremental package checks.
Fresh-process resume for two isolated projects preserved local pending work without modifying framework continuity.
Manual diff review completed; native Obsidian application and real product repositories were not exercised.
decisions: Upstream receives framework maintenance only; product sessions stay in their own repositories.
Preserve unbound legacy state for reconciliation rather than importing or erasing it.
Keep Obsidian views generated from canonical project memory; protect user edits.
pending_work: Reconcile and adopt isolated memory in individual real product repositories when working on them.
Continue context-efficiency stage 2 after this project-memory boundary improvement.
risks: No real product repository was migrated or tested in production.
Obsidian native application rendering was not tested; generated contents and isolation were verified.
Runtime instructions must invoke the lifecycle entry point; it is not a background recorder.
next_action: On the next product task, inspect its existing memory and initialize or reconcile its project-local identity before resuming work.
